claim: Vitamin D3 soft gel capsule (SGC) supplementation significantly raises circulating 25(OH)D levels in vitamin D-deficient adults, from a deficient baseline of ~12 ng/ml to sufficient levels of ~38 ng/ml over 6 weeks
stance_target: Vitamin D3 softgel capsule efficacy for correcting deficiency
scope_conditions: Prospective randomized clinical trial; Pakistan; n=20; healthy adults with VDD (<20 ng/ml); weekly 200,000 IU doses for 6 weeks
quoted_support: At 6-weeks follow-up, circulatory 25(OH)D levels showed a further considerable increase in the sucrosomial® Vit D3 treatment group to 66.1 ± 5.1 ng/ml, with a statistically significant difference in the SGC Vit D3 group (38.2 ± 2.6 ng/ml), which showed only a minimal increase.
numbers: SGC raised 25(OH)D from 12.6 ng/ml to 38.2 ng/ml at 6 weeks

claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation in all tested formulations (softgel, chewable tablet, sucrosomial) was well tolerated with no adverse events, no hypercalcemia, and no negative effects on liver enzymes or creatinine
stance_target: Safety of Vitamin D3 supplementation including softgel capsule form
scope_conditions: Two parallel RCTs, N=45 total, 6-week high-dose supplementation (200,000 IU/week = equivalent to ~28,000 IU/day during supplementation period), Pakistan 2023
quoted_support: Overall, in both studies, the Vit D3 treatment was well tolerated by all participants, and there were no treatment-related adverse effects, side effects, serious events, or discontinuation of the Vit D3 treatment due to safety reasons.
entities: Bano A et al. Front Nutr 2023

claim: Vitamin D deficiency (25(OH)D <20 ng/ml) prevalence is extremely high in South Asia: over one billion people worldwide are vitamin D deficient; Pakistan has 53.5% prevalence rate (63% in females), with similar patterns across India
stance_target: Need for Vitamin D supplementation in Indian population
scope_conditions: Global epidemiological data; VDD prevalence 20-90% in Europe, USA, Middle East; similar trends in India, Africa, South America
quoted_support: Approximately, over one billion people worldwide are Vit D deficient, and the deficiency is frequently undiagnosed. The prevalence of VDD in Europe, USA, and the Middle East ranges from 20 to 90%, with similar trends also reported in Australia, India, Africa, South America, Turkey, and Lebanon.
numbers: Over 1 billion people worldwide VD deficient
entities: Amrein K et al. Eur J Clin Nutr 2020

claim: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to rickets, osteomalacia, osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease, autoimmune diseases, depression, tuberculosis, and cancer beyond classic bone disorders
stance_target: Multi-benefit claims for Vitamin D3 supplementation
scope_conditions: Review of literature on VDD associations; multiple disease outcomes
quoted_support: Vit D deficiency (VDD), defined as circulatory 25(OH)D levels < 20 ng/ml, is not only linked with rickets or osteomalacia or osteoporosis but also with the risk of cardiovascular diseases, autoimmune diseases (such as type 1 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and multiple sclerosis), impaired mental health conditions (such as depression, anxiety, and Parkinson's disease), tuberculosis, and cancer (breast cancer and colon cancer).
entities: Janoušek J et al. Crit Rev Clin Lab Sci 2022

claim: Vitamin D3 has protective effects against respiratory tract infections and emerging evidence links VDD to COVID-19 severity and mortality
scope_conditions: Multiple studies; evidence ranges from experimental to observational to RCT data on respiratory infections
quoted_support: Vit D has also shown protective effects against respiratory tract infections, and there is emerging evidence of a possible association between VDD and progression to severe illness and mortality in patients with COVID-19. Circulatory Vit D levels affect the proliferation and differentiation of immune cells, and its deficiency results in impaired immune response.
numbers: Innate and adaptive immunity both modulated by vitamin D
